items.title: Launch HN: RonanRX (YC S26) – Personalized Peptides and GLP-1s
items.summary: Hi HN, I’m Lloyd, one of two founders of RonanRx ( https://ronanrx.com/ ). We are building a vertically integrated pharmaceutical company with software for prescribing, telehealth, compounding, manufacturing, and delivery. We are starting with GLP-1s and peptides. The path to RonanRx is fairly unconventional. During the pandemic, I built one of the largest mask manufacturing factories in the US. We could make a million masks in a day. We converted raw polypropylene pellets into finished pallets of masks. I had a background in software from my YC W10 company, so we took a software approach to building our factory. We used machine learning and computer vision to optimize production. We also vertically integrated almost everything. It worked. We built an efficient manufacturing operation and grew the business to 50 million dollars in revenue. Then people actually stopped caring about masks. Fair enough. Around the same time, I decided to try and lose the weight I had gained while building the factory. I ate nothing but chicken for six months. While this diet got some results, I plateaued. My doctor suggested tirzepatide, a GLP-1 medication. For me, losing weight was only the beginning. "Food noise" was gone. I showed less interest in other compulsive behavior. I stopped scrolling Instagram and quit biting my nails. But that was just the beginning. I was born with a congenital heart defect called aortic stenosis. My whole life doctors told me I'd need open heart surgery in my…

items.summary: Get your copy of Luke’s new book: A Horse Named Lonesome https://ahorsenamedlonesome.com The Neuroscience of Addiction, Breaking Bad Habits, Childhood Trauma, Psychedelic Healing, Loneliness & Emotional Recovery Host Dave Asprey sits down with Luke Storey, host of The Life Stylist Podcast and author of A Horse Named Lonesome, to explore the science of addiction, loneliness, childhood trauma, emotional healing, psychedelics, brain chemistry, and the surprising relationship between human connection and happiness. Drawing on nearly three decades of recovery from drug addiction, Luke explains why overcoming substance abuse doesn't necessarily resolve the emotional patterns behind it, how unresolved trauma can shape relationships and behavior, and why having fewer, deeper friendships may lead to greater fulfillment. Luke shares his journey from childhood trauma and early substance use to long-term sobriety, revealing why he continued struggling with codependency, unhealthy relationships, and self-destructive patterns even after 20 years without addictive drugs. He discusses his controversial decision to explore ayahuasca and other psychedelics after two decades of sobriety, the emotional breakthroughs he experienced, and the importance of distinguishing personal healing experiences from approaches that may be appropriate for others. Dave and Luke examine the relationship between addiction, trauma, altered states of consciousness, meditation, and the brain's ability to change…

items.title: MariTide Explained: Amgen's Once-Monthly GLP-1 Antibody Conjugate and Its Side Effects
items.summary: MariTide (maridebart cafraglutide, formerly AMG 133) is Amgen's investigational obesity drug: a fully human antibody that blocks the GIP receptor, linked to two GLP-1 agonist peptides, designed for once-monthly injection. This short covers how the dual mechanism works, what the Phase 1 trial and the 52-week Phase 2 trial in the New England Journal of Medicine showed on weight and blood sugar, where the Phase 3 MARITIME program stands, and what trials reported on side effects, from nausea and vomiting to GI dropouts and gallbladder events. Subscribe to Peptide Science Explained for more clear, science-backed breakdowns. Disclaimer: This video is for educational and informational purposes only and is not medical advice. Always consult a licensed healthcare provider before starting, stopping, or changing any treatment. #MariTide #GLP1 #peptides

items.title: Petrelintide Explained: The Long-Acting Amylin Analogue and Its Side Effects
items.summary: Petrelintide is a once-weekly peptide modeled on human amylin, a satiety hormone co-secreted with insulin. Zealand Pharma designed it; Roche and Genentech are co-developing it. This short covers how the amylin pathway differs from GLP-1 drugs, what the Phase 2 ZUPREME-1 trial showed on weight and cardiometabolic markers, the Phase 3 ZUPREME program now underway, and what trials reported on side effects, from mild nausea to placebo-like gut tolerability. items.title: Mazdutide Explained: The GLP-1 and Glucagon Dual Agonist and Its Side Effects
items.summary: Mazdutide is a once-weekly peptide modeled on oxyntomodulin that activates both the GLP-1 and glucagon receptors. In 2025 China approved it for chronic weight management and type 2 diabetes, the first dual glucagon/GLP-1 agonist approved for weight loss. This short covers how it works, what the GLORY-1, GLORY-2, and DREAMS-3 trials and Lilly's U.S. phase 2 trial showed, where it stands outside China, and what trials reported on side effects, from nausea and vomiting to heart rate and gallbladder findings. Subscribe to Peptide Science Explained for more clear, science-backed breakdowns. Disclaimer: This video is for educational and informational purposes only and is not medical advice. Always consult a licensed healthcare provider before starting, stopping, or changing any treatment. #mazdutide #GLP1 #peptides
